taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Akpoku, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 790.38 | 0.36897 | 0.36897
2 | 1854.8 | 0.8832 | 0.45729
3 | 2133.7 | 3.7316 | 4.1889
4 | 747.1 | 28.838 | 33.027
5 | 1230.6 | 48.108 | 81.135
6 | 2200.9 | - | -

What is the curve type of this station? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the curve-type notation for the Akpoku station, we examine the resistivity values of the layers in order:

1.  **Layer 1:** 790.38 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$
2.  **Layer 2:** 1854.8 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$
3.  **Layer 3:** 2133.7 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$
4.  **Layer 4:** 747.1 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$
5.  **Layer 5:** 1230.6 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$
6.  **Layer 6:** 2200.9 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$

Next, we evaluate each group of three consecutive layers:

*   **Group 1 (Layers 1-2-3):** 790.38 < 1854.8 < 2133.7. This follows the pattern $r_1 < r_2 < r_3$, which is **A**.
*   **Group 2 (Layers 2-3-4):** 1854.8 < 2133.7 > 747.1. This follows the pattern $r_1 < r_2 > r_3$, which is **K**.
*   **Group 3 (Layers 3-4-5):** 2133.7 > 747.1 < 1230.6. This follows the pattern $r_1 > r_2 < r_3$, which is **H**.
*   **Group 4 (Layers 4-5-6):** 747.1 < 1230.6 < 2200.9. This follows the pattern $r_1 < r_2 < r_3$, which is **A**.

Combining these letters in order gives the curve type AKHA.

{"curve_type": "AKHA"}
